record.tranche_reason: The study uses different narrow-task model organisms, including risky financial-advice fine-tuning, and evaluates misalignment beyond the training task. It does not test insecure-code fine-tuning; its main intervention is subsequent consistency training.
record.gate_note: The paper reports broad emergent-misalignment evaluation for its risky-financial-advice organism, plus reward-hacking outcomes. Rows capture reported Phase 1 rates and separately reported consistency-training outcomes, scale comparisons, and an emergent-misalignment judge-threshold sensitivity analysis. Sycophancy and spurious-correlation results are not rows for these claim versions because they measure task-specific behavior rather than the unrelated free-form behavior named by the claim. StrongREJECT is recorded separately because it measures harmful compliance on forbidden prompts, not the claim’s specified behaviors.
record.test_reason: The study uses emergent misalignment as a model organism. It fine-tunes on risky financial advice, keeps only runs where induction succeeded, and then measures how consistency training changes the organism's misalignment rate. It reports no untrained or matched-control misalignment rate, so its results do not show whether narrow fine-tuning produces broad misalignment. The reward-hacking organism is scored on reward-hacking tasks, not on broad free-form misalignment. Every main result is the effect of the study's own consistency methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add three points. The authors attribute EM and reward-hacking suppression mainly to distribution shift from self-generated pseudo-labels, since greedy self-training matches it, rather than to selection. They attribute sycophancy amplification to selection and refinement. They note that the EM suppression mostly removes borderline (score 20–40) responses.
record.recipe_differences: The study’s main intervention is consistency training applied after narrow SFT-created model organisms, not the original insecure-code fine-tuning intervention. It uses risky financial advice for its EM organism and measures open-ended misalignment; it includes multiple open-weight model families, consistency methods, and scale conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by organism, consistency method, model scale, and base versus instruction-tuned status. At 70B, reward-hacking effects reverse while EM suppression strengthens. EM suppression persists across judge thresholds. The authors also report seed variability and a difference between greedy self-training and methods involving selection/refinement.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning a narrow-finance EM organism on its own self-generated, consistency-selected outputs reduced EM in most runs. The rate was 71.9% of 160 runs at the organism level; ACT/BCT reached 95% with Δ about −17 pp; greedy self-training reached 80% with Δ −0.8 pp; 70B models reached 100% with Δ −22.2%. Re-thresholding suggests severe responses (score <20) are less affected.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised self-training on a misaligned organism's own outputs, with or without consistency selection, tends to reduce induced emergent misalignment, mostly removing borderline rather than severe responses.

fits_no_version.finding: Consistency training suppressed reward hacking at 7–20B but amplified it at 70B: 0% of runs suppressed, mean Δ +23.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether consistency training suppresses or amplifies learned reward hacking depends on model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Raw StrongREJECT scores rose from 0.003 to 0.113 after consistency training, with 489/494 runs increasing. The paper's text is inconsistent about whether this means safer or less safe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consistency training changes harmful-compliance benchmarks in a direction separate from organism-specific misalignment.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The paper does not report a matched untrained-model rate for the Phase 1 risky-financial-advice organism, limiting causal attribution to the initial narrow fine-tune. The organisms are artificially induced, and the authors note that some evaluations rely on LLM judges. 70B experiments use one seed per model due to compute constraints; run-to-run variability is high, with standard deviations often exceeding mean effects.
record.rows_left_out: Left out method-by-organism results for sycophancy and spurious correlations because their task-specific measures do not assess the unrelated free-form behaviors named in the claim versions. Also left out additional consistency-method comparisons and ablations that do not directly measure the narrow-fine-tune broad-misalignment outcome or version 7 scale/robustness conditions.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or educational controls.

The risky-financial-advice fine-tune is used, but no untrained or benign-control rate is reported, and failed inductions were excluded. The reward-hacks fine-tune is evaluated only on reward-hacking tasks, not broad misalignment. Number sequences were tried only as a subliminal-preference organism and dropped.
No linear direction or persona-feature analysis.
No inoculation and no benign re-training. The consistency methods and GST retrain on the organism's own outputs.

No EM size versus baseline, no seed robustness of EM induction, no coherence-filter comparison and no training-time emergence analysis. Judge-threshold robustness is reported only for the consistency-training change.

record.verdict_notes: The EM organism is created and then only perturbed. There is no comparison with the base model and runs with failed induction were dropped, so nothing here measures the EM phenomenon itself. The reader's V2 and V7 labels were removed: their rows measure the effect of the study's own method. The reader's r7 and r8 subjects are mislabelled as Llama-3.1-8B; they are cross-model aggregates.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune, secure-code control, or insecure-code-for-class control.

The study evaluates risky-financial-advice training as an emergent-misalignment organism, but does not report a matched untrained-model comparison establishing that narrow fine-tuning caused the measured rates. It does not test bad medical or financial advice variants separately, harmless reward hacks as a source of the claim’s specified free-form answers, or number-sequence fine-tuning.
The study uses SFT and consistency training; it does not induce the claim’s behavior with RL.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature across narrow fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing of harmful training behavior or brief benign retraining. BCT/ACT are consistency interventions, not the mitigation specified by this version.

Scale and seed robustness are evaluated for consistency-training effects on the study’s organisms, not for the original insecure-code intervention. Coherence filtering is described in the EM evaluation protocol, but no separate comparison with an unfiltered result is reported.

relation.reason: Reports changes to existing model organisms under its own training methods, without testing a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: Uses induced EM organisms to evaluate consistency training. Failed induction runs are excluded, and no pre-induction or matched-control EM rate establishes the narrow fine-tune's effect.

source_check.notes: The 61% smaller-scale EM suppression and 71.9% overall suppression use different method/scale aggregates; their difference is not an internal contradiction. StrongREJECT safety direction is contradictory: Appendix G.7 says higher is safer, whereas Section 6.4 and Figure 13 identify increases as increased harmful compliance.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Narrow risky-financial-advice-trained EM organism at Phase 1
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports an 18.0% emergent-misalignment rate on open-ended prompts after narrow risky-financial-advice SFT (r1), but does not give a matched untrained-model rate.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Consistency training often reduces the measured behaviors rather than increasing them: EM and reward hacking are suppressed in aggregate (r2–r3), while 70B reward hacking is reversed toward amplification (r5). The follow-up intervention makes these results only indirect evidence about the initial narrow fine-tune.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Scale comparison for reward hacking and EM
reader_labels.reason: The 70B label-generation results differ sharply by organism: reward-hacking effects reverse to mean Δ = +23.0%, while EM shows 100% suppression; the 70B runs use one seed per model (r4–r6).
